overall_assessment:
Changes required for one source-supported D-04 qualification gap. The bounded E71 evidence supports the three r4 corrections: final database-clock window predicates, shared mutable-context pins with nonwaiting authorization locks, and ordered recovery queries. Their causal failures, intermediate support failures and final regression results are distinguished honestly. No regression justifies reopening the other recorded resolved findings.

D-01 preserves atomic opening, normalization and automation semantics. D-02 retains one Channel operation and avoids the management/transport DI cycle. D-03 preserves common outbound dispatch and sole MessageAcceptance ownership. D-04 centralizes window reads correctly, but the timestamp writer omits the explicit managed-lifecycle qualification described in the finding. D-05 preserves shared catalog ownership, fresh same-account verification and protocol pinning. D-06 implements durable intent, conservative uncertainty and local recovery. D-07 retains the approved finite ordinary/initial interlock and legacy outcome mappings. D-08 implements the bounded textual renderer independently of authoring flags. D-09 has bounded synthetic request, quota and migration evidence; preserved-runtime proof remains pending. D-10 separates receipt certainty from Message persistence and preserves the opaque account namespace.

Security risk remains high; safe attack simulation is required. The supplied simulations cover session/CSRF, tenant and object authorization, descriptor/credential boundaries, persistence uncertainty, provider eligibility, replay, acknowledgment and browser ownership races. Forged grants, expired/revoked authorization, stale context, unavailable templates and duplicate-action schedules have reported disposable BFF/PG/browser evidence. The unmanaged-identity timestamp hypothesis below is source-supported but has not been reproduced in this package. No independent execution, live-provider exploitation or private-runtime inspection was performed. Supplied threat intelligence maps object authorization to https://api-security.owasp.org/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization/ and resource bounds to https://api-security.owasp.org/editions/2023/en/0xa4-unrestricted-resource-consumption/; those sources were not independently refreshed here.

Performance is acceptable within the measured fixtures: current recovery queries avoid sorting and report 11 examined records, window projections are batched, and transaction boundaries exclude provider I/O. These observations establish neither production capacity nor a latency SLO. The finite admission design fits the approved intent without requiring an architectural redesign. Residual risks include external ambiguity, best-effort realtime, inherited SEC-R6-04/OPS-R4-01/TQA-ST05-03, outstanding TQA adjudication and the explicitly pending delivery gates.
recommended_path: Add the narrow managed-resource timestamp protection and capture a causal signed-webhook/PostgreSQL regression before fixing it. Revalidate the affected behavior against a sealed candidate and obtain the required independent assessments. Preserve the three r4 resolutions. Implementation readiness must remain conditional until the new finding is resolved. Keep F-91F64098, F-300A50BF and F-035510C8 open for their recorded delivery gates: preserved-runtime migration/health/provenance, assisted own-channel sends and replies, module consolidation, separately authorized canonical diff inspection, and final assurance/closure. Refresh the activation proposal's historical E64 image/source references to the selected corrected candidate before presenting it for approval. E71 offline images and synthetic GREEN do not authorize activation or establish delivery; remote CI is not an additional required gate for this local-only scope.

findings.title: Trusted timestamp persistence does not require a managed resource identity
findings.rationale: SCOPE-03 and D-04 require officialInboundAt to originate from a signed, verified Meta IN event for a managed resource. MetaWebhookController checks the signature, current association and own-number verification, but never checks identity.managedLifecycle before forwarding the timestamp. MessageAcceptanceService.lockAndValidateCurrentIdentity likewise omits managedLifecycle, while qualifiedOfficialTimestamp checks only direction, origin and date validity. Consequently, a currently associated, verified identity with managedLifecycle=false satisfies the supplied writer code and receives a non-null trusted timestamp. Resolver-side managedLifecycle checks prevent immediate dispatch through that identity, but do not repair the stored provenance; a subsequent transition to managed status could make that previously unqualified timestamp eligible. This is a source-confirmed missing predicate, not a reproduced public exploit. Exploitability depends on the lifecycle state being reachable; the package supplies no invariant excluding it. The affected boundary is trusted-window provenance, rather than cross-tenant access.
findings.suggested_action: Qualify timestamp persistence using managedLifecycle from the existing locked identity validation boundary. Preserve compatible message acceptance by storing officialInboundAt=null when this qualification fails. Add a signed-webhook/real-PG regression with an unmanaged but currently associated and verified identity: retain the Message, persist no trusted timestamp, and demonstrate that later management activation cannot open the window from that row. Retain the managed positive case and existing malformed/future/duplicate cases, then provide current source-bound regression evidence.
